THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR HEARING ON 26.11.2025, THE COURT ON 04.12.2025 DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:93314 MACA No.2587/2012  ..2..

1  JUDGMENT

This appeal has been filed by the claimant in OP(MV) No.172 of 2006 on the files of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tirur, a claim petition filed under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, "the Act"), challenging the dismissal of the claim petition.
The respondents herein were the respondents before the tribunal.

2. The case of the claimant is that on 26.04.2004, while he was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-1-OP-3292, the front wheel of the motorcycle was burst, resulting in the vehicle capsizing, whereby he sustained serious injuries.
He approached the tribunal claiming compensation.
The first respondent/owner of the motorcycle appeared before the tribunal.
The second respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy coverage for the offending vehicle, but disputing the liability and quantum of compensation claimed.
It was contended that the claimant was not covered under the policy as no additional premium was paid.
PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A21, B1, B2 & C1 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, dismissed the claim petition, relying on United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Vijayaraja [2009 (3) KLT 269], wherein this Court held that the claims petition under Section 2025:KER:93314 ..3..
163A is not maintainable when the rider was using the motorcycle with the permission of the registered owner and by his own negligence caused the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Challenging the dismissal of the claim petition, the claimant has come up in appeal.
3. I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurer.

4. The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the tribunal went wrong in dismissing the claim petition since the rider of the vehicle, who would step into the shoes of the owner, would be entitled for personal accident coverage.

5. The learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurer, relying on the judgment of the apex court in Ramkhiladi & another v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & others [2020 KHC 6008],
wherein it was held that the claim petition under Section 163-A is not maintainable by borrower/permissive user of vehicle against owner and/or insurer of said vehicle, as such borrower/permissive user steps into shoes of owner, and owner cannot both be claimant and recipient, and further submitted that the tribunal is right in dismissing the claim petition.
6.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi & another v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & others [2020 KHC 6008]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
I have considered the rival contentions raised on both 2025:KER:93314 ..4..
sides.
I find force in the argument put forward by the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company.
There is no dispute to the fact that the deceased was the rider of the motorcycle.

As per the judgment in Ramkhiladi (supra), since the claimant was the rider of the motorcycle, he would step into the shoes of the owner, and is not entitled to claim any compensation from the insurer of the vehicle.

In the present case, a perusal of the copy of the insurance policy handed over A.Sreejayan vs Sukumaran*(Dismissed) on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6133862/
2 to me by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant shows that no additional premium is paid to cover the risk of the owner/rider; and hence, the claimant is not entitled for any compensation.

Further, the injuries sustained by the appellant do not come under notified injuries for claiming personal accident coverage such as, loss of limb, amputation or any injury that temporarily or permanently prevents him from carrying out his work.
Therefore, I hold that the tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition and therefore, the impugned award does not require any interference.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.

Sd/-
SHOBA ANNAMMA EAPEN JUDGE bka/-
